units.source_excerpt: The rapid growth of tourism has led many countries and regions to recognize the tension between environmental preservation and the short-term economic benefits of traditional tourism models.
units.function: Open with a domain-wide tension before localizing the case.

features.clause_structure: causal main clause followed by between-coordination
features.quantitative_role: names the competing dimensions before equations

units.reusable_pattern: [Long-run trend] has exposed the tension between [objective A] and [objective B].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim that every destination has the same conflict.
Do not copy the tourism-specific nouns when adapting the pattern.

units.source_excerpt: This paper develops a multi-objective planning model that integrates economic, social, and environmental factors, tailored to the current state of the tourism industry in Juneau and its development goals.
units.function: State the artifact, its three dimensions, and its local scope in one sentence.

features.clause_structure: main action plus relative integration and participial scope phrase

units.reusable_pattern: This paper develops [model class] that integrates [dimensions], tailored to [case state and goals].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not imply that integration proves commensurability.
Do not retain the city name in another case.

units.source_excerpt: In Sub-model I, economic benefit is the primary optimization objective. Considering the diminishing marginal returns and increasing marginal costs associated with a rising number of tourists, we developed a mathematical relationship between economic benefits and costs as a function of tourist volume.
units.function: Launch the first parallel branch with objective, mechanisms, and response variable.

features.voice: active first-person plural after research-object opening
features.clause_structure: short objective sentence plus fronted mechanism phrase
features.quantitative_role: maps tourist volume to benefit and cost

units.reusable_pattern: In Sub-model [i], [quantity] is the [ordinal] objective. Considering [mechanisms], we model [output] as a function of [driver].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call an assumed curve empirical.
Do not copy the ordinal when objectives are not ranked.

units.source_excerpt: Through a cost-benefit analysis (CBA) model, we then defined the feasible domain of economic constraints and determined the maximum economic benefit.
units.function: Close a branch with method, feasible set, and optimized output.

features.clause_structure: fronted method phrase plus coordinated actions
features.quantitative_role: links analysis to constraint and optimum

units.reusable_pattern: Through [method], we define [feasible domain] and determine [conditional optimum].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not describe a searched point as global without evidence.
Do not omit the governing constraints.

units.source_excerpt: In Sub-model II, social benefit is the second optimization objective. It is assessed through social satisfaction analysis and monetization. Social satisfaction is influenced by residents' living pressure and regional congestion.
units.function: Repeat the branch skeleton while changing the measurement bridge.

features.clause_structure: three short sentences with repeated subject

units.reusable_pattern: In Sub-model [ii], [objective] is assessed through [indicator analysis] and [conversion]. [Indicator] is influenced by [factor A] and [factor B].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a proxy observed satisfaction without survey data.
Do not assume monetization is objective.

units.source_excerpt: In Sub-model III, environmental benefit is the third optimization objective. Focusing on glacier degradation, the primary environmental issue in Juneau, we chose the carbon footprint as the key environmental indicator.
units.function: Move from local environmental concern to one operational indicator.

features.clause_structure: branch sentence plus fronted focus phrase

units.reusable_pattern: Focusing on [case-specific harm], we use [measurable proxy] as the environmental indicator.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not equate the proxy with the full environmental system.
Do not infer glacier causation from local visitor emissions alone.

units.source_excerpt: Furthermore, we integrate the three preceding models and account for the coupling relationships among them. Using the SLSQP method, we determine the global Pareto-optimal solution for tourist numbers and overall benefits.
units.function: Converge the parallel branches into one solver stage.

features.clause_structure: integration sentence plus fronted solver phrase

units.reusable_pattern: Furthermore, we integrate the preceding [branches]. Using [solver], we determine [decision variables] under [combined constraints].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call one weighted-sum point a Pareto front.
Do not claim globality from a local solver.

units.source_excerpt: Specifically, when the number of tourists reaches 1.32 million, the economic measure of the municipal weighted total benefit is 10 million USD, while the net income for Juneau amounts to 576 million USD.
units.function: Attach the decision point to two named output scales.
units.reusable_pattern: Specifically, at [decision value], [objective output] is [value], while [comparison output] is [value].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not mix weighted and unweighted totals without labels.
Do not preserve unsupported significant digits.

units.source_excerpt: Finally, we analyze the sensitivity of key model parameters, as well as the sources of additional government revenue and spending programs.
units.function: Signal the final analytical checks and feedback topic.
units.reusable_pattern: Finally, we examine [sensitivity dimensions], together with [implementation or feedback topic].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not imply that listing expenditures closes a model feedback loop.
Do not call one-factor curves full robustness.

units.source_excerpt: We also write a memo to the Tourist Council of Juneau and extend the model to Jiuzhaigou, China.
units.function: Close by naming communication and transfer deliverables.
units.reusable_pattern: We also translate the analysis into [stakeholder artifact] and transfer it to [second context].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim transfer validity merely because equations are reused.
Do not copy the destination names.

units.source_excerpt: In recent years, tourism has played an increasingly significant role in driving local economic growth, generating substantial revenue and gradually becoming a pillar industry for both local and global economies. However, with the continuous rise in tourist numbers, issues such as environmental degradation, increased infrastructure costs, and declining resident satisfaction have emerged.
units.function: Establish the benefit-to-pressure reversal in the domain.

features.clause_structure: benefit accumulation followed by However reversal

units.reusable_pattern: [Activity] has supported [benefits]. However, as [driver] rises, [cost A], [cost B], and [cost C] emerge.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not convert a general trend into causation without evidence.
Do not reuse tourism-specific facts.

units.source_excerpt: Juneau is renowned for its unique and breathtaking natural landscapes, which include expansive national parks, majestic glaciers, and a 6,640-mile coastline. These attractions draw hundreds of thousands to over a million tourists annually, with the majority arriving via luxury cruise ships.
units.function: Localize the broad conflict with place, scale, and transport mode.

features.clause_structure: relative asset list followed by quantitative context

units.reusable_pattern: [Case] is characterized by [assets]. These attract [scale], primarily through [channel], producing [benefit] alongside [pressure].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not transplant Juneau statistics.
Do not use scenic adjectives as evidence.

units.source_excerpt: To mitigate the negative impacts of unsustainable tourism growth, the Juneau government has implemented measures such as raising taxes and limiting visitor numbers to regulate tourist flow. Additionally, it has intensified efforts to promote alternative attractions.
units.function: Move from diagnosed pressure to existing policy responses and remaining need.

features.clause_structure: purpose infinitive plus examples and addition

units.reusable_pattern: To mitigate [harm], [actor] has implemented [measures]. Moving forward, the remaining task is to balance [objectives].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present proposed measures as evaluated outcomes.
Do not omit who controls the levers.

units.source_excerpt: Based on the current situation in Juneau and the information outlined in the problem statement, it is essential to develop a comprehensive sustainable tourism management plan to maximize economic, social, and environmental benefits. Specifically, the plan must address the following three issues.
units.function: Bridge context into a finite task inventory.

features.clause_structure: based-on frame plus infinitive and inventory preview

units.reusable_pattern: Based on [case evidence] and [task source], the plan must address the following [n] issues.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add requirements not present in the prompt.
Do not claim comprehensiveness before clause tracing.

units.source_excerpt: Problem 1: Develop a sustainable tourism management model tailored to the specific context of Juneau, considering all factors that may influence the long-term sustainable tourism industry.
units.function: Turn the first official deliverable into a scope-controlled modeling clause.

features.clause_structure: imperative verb plus participial scope clause

units.reusable_pattern: Problem [i]: Develop [artifact] for [case], considering [named factor classes].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not substitute all factors for a concrete factor list.
Do not merge transfer and communication deliverables here.

units.source_excerpt: Problem 2: Extend the model to other cities negatively affected by tourism and demonstrate its applicability in these cities. Problem 3: Based on the model developed in Problem 1, submit a one page memo to the Juneau Tourism Commission.
units.function: Keep transfer and stakeholder communication as distinct downstream branches.
units.reusable_pattern: Problem [ii] transfers [artifact]; Problem [iii], based on [earlier output], communicates [decision content] to [audience].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat transfer as validation.
Do not let the memo introduce new results.

units.source_excerpt: The main indicators of the relevant discussions focus on the environmental, economic and social aspects. In the existing studies, some scholars analyze the environmental benefits of tourism development, while others discuss long-term social-economic stability and quality of life.
units.function: Organize literature by the same dimensions used later in the model.
units.reusable_pattern: Existing studies divide into [dimension A], [dimension B], and [dimension C], with one stream addressing [topic] while another addresses [topic].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use citation lists without proposition-level links.
Do not imply consensus from a few sources.

units.source_excerpt: However, the models that introduce Pareto optimization into sustainable tourism management and comprehensively consider the economic, social and environmental tripartite benefits are still few.
units.function: End the review with a precise combination gap that motivates the paper architecture.

features.clause_structure: However contrast plus restrictive relative clause

units.reusable_pattern: However, studies combining [method] with [all required dimensions] remain limited; we therefore introduce [method] into [model class].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call the combination innovative without systematic search.
Do not infer correctness from novelty.

units.source_excerpt: Our Work: Analysis of Model Applicability to Other Cities; Sensitivity Analysis; Tourism Management Solution; Memo to the Tourist Council of Juneau.
units.function: Preview the end-to-end workflow as a visual dependency map.
units.reusable_pattern: Preview [inputs] -> [parallel model branches] -> [integration] -> [validation/transfer] -> [decision artifact].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not let a workflow arrow substitute for an implemented feedback edge.
Do not omit official deliverables.

units.source_excerpt: Assumption 1: Demand and expenditure exhibit increasing marginal utility, while revenue (including hidden costs) follows decreasing marginal returns. Justification: This aligns with classical economic models characterizing resource-constrained benefit-cost curves.
units.function: Pair a curve-shape assumption immediately with its modeling purpose.

features.clause_structure: while contrast followed by labeled justification

units.reusable_pattern: Assumption [i]: [formal behavior]. Justification: [why it is useful and what simplification it creates].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call the assumption observed unless fitted.
Do not use increasing marginal utility when the equation encodes something else.

units.source_excerpt: Assumption 2: Hidden costs, such as infrastructure strain and carbon footprint, are monetized in USD. Justification: This provides dimensional consistency for quantitative analysis.
units.function: Expose the commensurability assumption before scalarization.

features.clause_structure: labeled assumption plus short purpose justification

units.reusable_pattern: Assume [heterogeneous effects] can be expressed in [common unit] so that [operation] is dimensionally defined.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not infer valid shadow prices from unit consistency.
Do not hide double counting.

units.source_excerpt: Assumption 3: Tourist spending or policy changes instantaneously affect visitor numbers. Justification: This assumes a full-information market, simplifying tourism's inherent time-lag dynamics.
units.function: Name the dynamic behavior removed by the static model.
units.reusable_pattern: Assume [response] is instantaneous, removing [lag/process]; record [extension] as the boundary.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not narrate a static model as a forecast.
Do not say elasticity alone repairs missing dynamics.

units.source_excerpt: Assumption 4: Parameters are spatiotemporally localized, ignoring external competition, infrastructure decay, or seasonal fluctuations. Justification: Focusing on Juneau's internal resource allocation efficiency, this supports short-term partial equilibrium analysis.
units.function: Close assumptions with an explicit exclusion list and time horizon.
units.reusable_pattern: Parameters are localized to [case/time], excluding [mechanisms]; therefore interpret results as [scope].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim long-term sustainability from a short-term equilibrium.
Do not omit seasonality when it drives demand.

units.source_excerpt: Table 1: Variations and Parameters. Economic Notations; Social Notations; Environmental Notations.
units.function: Group symbols by the same three objective branches used in the model.
units.reusable_pattern: Organize notation as [shared variables] followed by one band per model branch, with units adjacent.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave percentage/proportion conventions ambiguous.
Do not call decision variables parameters.

Do not omit parameter units and domains.

units.source_excerpt: Economic benefits is the first core objective of local tourism development. An increase in the number of tourists not only promotes local economic growth and increases municipal revenues, but also provides more employment opportunities for local residents.
units.function: Open a submodel by explaining why its objective matters to named stakeholders.
units.reusable_pattern: [Objective] is a core objective because [driver] affects [stakeholder A] through [channel] and [stakeholder B] through [channel].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not infer net benefit from gross revenue channels.
Do not rank objectives without a stated basis.

units.source_excerpt: Maximization of economic benefits can be expressed as follows: max E = CGi - CGc, where CGi represents visible economic revenues and CGc is the increase in public-service and infrastructure costs.
units.function: Place the objective equation immediately before variable interpretation.

features.transition: can be expressed as follows; where

units.reusable_pattern: [Optimization direction] of [objective] is [equation], where [term] represents [meaning] and [term] represents [meaning].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use E for both economic and total objectives without clarification.
Do not omit units.

units.source_excerpt: The direct consumption generated by tourists is most significantly influenced by the number of tourists, so it can be regarded as a linear function of the number of tourists. Therefore, the formula for calculating direct consumption is given by Ct = alpha times Nt.
units.function: Move from dominant driver to a base equation, then refine its coefficient.

features.clause_structure: causal so clause followed by Therefore formula lead-in

units.reusable_pattern: Because [output] is chiefly driven by [input], begin with [base relation]; then let [coefficient] vary with [mechanism].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call the base relation empirical without fit evidence.
Do not insert a dimensioned exponent.

units.source_excerpt: A portion of the consumption generated by tourists is used to pay municipal taxes, while the other portion is used to purchase tourism-related goods and services provided by local residents. Therefore, Ct = CGi + CRi.
units.function: Translate a stakeholder narrative into a conservation-style decomposition.
units.reusable_pattern: Partition [total flow] into [stakeholder share A] and [stakeholder share B], then express the identity and allocation rule.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assume all spending remains local.
Do not mix tax as percent and proportion.

units.source_excerpt: The components of economic costs are more complex than economic revenues. On the one hand, Juneau needs fixed expenditures on public services every year. On the other hand, increased tourists accelerate infrastructure damage.
units.function: Introduce a cost equation through fixed-versus-volume-dependent components.

features.clause_structure: On the one hand/On the other hand pairing
features.transition: On the one hand; On the other hand; Therefore

units.reusable_pattern: Decompose cost into [fixed component] and [driver-dependent component]; use [shape] to encode [marginal behavior].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not choose a quadratic solely because it creates an interior optimum.
Do not omit coefficient provenance.

units.source_excerpt: Considering the two key economic principles of diminishing marginal benefits and increasing marginal costs, it can be hypothesized that the government should have two break-even points. The break-even point is the point at which economic benefits equal economic costs.
units.function: Interpret equation shapes through thresholds and a viable domain.
units.reusable_pattern: Considering [opposing marginal effects], define [threshold] where [terms balance], then interpret the interval as [decision domain].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim two roots without verifying the equations and domain.
Do not treat a schematic curve as data.

units.source_excerpt: The social benefits is the second key objective that we analyze in our models. When the number of tourists is too high, local residents feel more pressure due to living costs and congestion; when it is too low, tourism-service income may decline.
units.function: Motivate a middle-range objective through two-sided stakeholder pressure.

features.clause_structure: when high/on the contrary when low contrast
features.transition: When; On the contrary; Combining; Ultimately

units.reusable_pattern: At high [driver], [harm A] rises; at low [driver], [harm B] rises. Combine them into [objective].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assume an interior optimum without checking the formula.
Do not infer satisfaction from income alone.

units.source_excerpt: Residents' social satisfaction is mainly determined by two mutually constraining factors: pressure on living and pressure on congestion. Thus, the dimensionless indicator of social satisfaction s can be denoted as s = Pl times Pf.
units.function: Name two components, define each, then combine them multiplicatively.
units.reusable_pattern: Define [indicator] from [component A] and [component B]; after stating each direction, combine them as [operation].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not multiply components without checking units and monotonicity.
Do not label an inverse crowding ratio pressure without clarifying direction.

units.source_excerpt: We use the virtual economic benefits generated by unit social satisfaction as an equivalent quantitative indicator. Specifically, the monetized conversion includes two steps: the hidden economic benefit equivalent per unit and the total hidden economic benefit generated by satisfaction.
units.function: Make the conversion bridge explicit as a two-step calculation.

features.clause_structure: purpose explanation plus Specifically numbered preview

units.reusable_pattern: To place [nonmonetary indicator] in a common objective, define [unit equivalent] and then compute [total equivalent].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a virtual equivalent measured welfare.
Do not omit how the conversion parameter is identified.

units.source_excerpt: In Model II, we combine the stress of living in Juneau with the stress of overcrowding and obtain the social benefit equivalent by measuring satisfaction through a virtual economic value. It can be assumed that social benefits are acceptable when more than 60% of residents achieve satisfaction.
units.function: Close the social branch by restating construction and defining acceptability.

features.quantitative_role: defines S greater than 0.6 times baseline
features.transition: In Model II; Since; That is

units.reusable_pattern: In [model], combine [components] to obtain [objective]; use [baseline/criterion] to define the acceptable domain.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not confuse percent satisfied with 60% of a constructed benefit.
Do not call the baseline independent validation.

units.source_excerpt: Environmental damage has significant hidden economic costs for the tourism industry and increases potential government expenditures. In order to quantitatively assess the hidden economic costs, we account for the carbon footprint of attractions and conduct an economization analysis.
units.function: Translate environmental harm into the paper's common objective language.

features.voice: environmental damage as subject then active we

units.reusable_pattern: Because [harm] creates [hidden cost], use [proxy] and [conversion] to define [environmental objective].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call environmental cost benefit.
Do not present carbon as the entire environmental system.

units.source_excerpt: Since the primary cause of glacier melt is temperature increase, the glacier recession equation summarized for assessing the recession of Mendenhall Glacier is as follows. This formula is only used to predict the melting rate and is not added to the environmental benefit evaluation model, but replaced by carbon emission.

features.clause_structure: Since premise plus formula lead-in and but exclusion

prohibited_generalizations: Do not call an unused equation part of the optimizer.
Do not infer local glacier response from global climate sensitivity without units.

units.source_excerpt: We take into account that changes in the number of visitors to different attractions may lead to different carbon emissions, and analyze the carbon emissions of different attractions separately. From this, the total carbon emissions can be expressed as the sum of individual emissions.
units.function: Move from attraction-level allocation to an aggregate environmental input.

features.clause_structure: take-into-account clause plus From this aggregation

Do not label concentration effects empirical without calibration.

units.source_excerpt: For Cenv, we use tax to reflect the government's additional revenue; for CCO2, first estimate the virtual cost equivalent per unit of carbon emissions, and then calculate the potential economic loss due to environmental pollution.
units.function: Build the environmental balance from governance input and carbon-loss output.

features.clause_structure: for A/for B parallelism with first-then sequence

prohibited_generalizations: Do not omit the carbon price source.

units.source_excerpt: The formulation exhibits a dual structure balancing government-led environmental investments against dispersed carbon emission costs. Conversely, the carbon cost aggregation inherently penalizes concentrated tourism patterns through its quadratic summation structure.
units.function: Interpret the two nonlinear branches and extract the policy logic.
units.reusable_pattern: The formulation balances [beneficial mechanism] against [cost mechanism]; one saturates while the other grows with [concentration].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not describe encoded behavior as observed mechanism.
Do not claim environmental effectiveness without data.

units.source_excerpt: From the analysis in the preceding three sections, expressions for economic, social, and environmental benefits can be derived respectively. The total benefit is formulated as a weighted average of these three dimensions, yielding the following optimization objective.
units.function: Converge three parallel branches into a single objective after recapping each direction.
units.reusable_pattern: From the preceding [n] branches, collect [objectives] and combine them through [declared aggregation rule].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call fixed scalarization Pareto optimization by itself.
Do not combine incompatible units without a justified normalization.

units.source_excerpt: Additionally, the constraints are formulated as follows: E > 0, S > Smin, Env < 0, T > 0, and Ntmax > Nt > 0. Smin denotes the minimum social benefit that Juneau can sustain, based on the social benefit in 2023.

units.source_excerpt: The weights for economic, social, and environmental benefits are derived from state-level reference metrics. This methodology assumes that a lower ranking in a specific dimension indicates a greater demand for improvement in that dimension, thus justifying a higher assigned weight.
units.function: Explain the normative rule that maps external ranks into objective weights.

prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat unrelated rankings as stakeholder preferences.
Do not invert rank direction without checking meaning.

units.source_excerpt: Economic, social and environmental benefits usually form a competitive relationship. This competition is typically influenced by multiple factors, such as the number of tourists and tax rates.

units.source_excerpt: Specifically, by solving the Multi-Objective Programming Model using the SLSQP method, under the above constraints, we can obtain a Pareto optimal solution where the benefits are most reasonably allocated.

units.source_excerpt: In the model, we try to analyze and optimize the total maximization of benefits by finding the optimal number of tourists, in which the economic, social and environmental benefits are all within the acceptable domain as the main constraints.

units.source_excerpt: We traverse the number of tourists in the range of 0-10 million, and through the coupled analysis of social, economic, and environmental benefits, we conclude that the total benefits is maximized when the total number of tourists is 1.32 million.

units.source_excerpt: Infrastructure management and operation expenditure; Environmental maintenance expenditure; Expenditures on the management of environmental damage.
units.function: Separate preventive, operating, and remedial spending channels.
units.reusable_pattern: For each spending channel, state timing, target state, model parameter affected, and expected decision effect.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim an effect without mapping expenditure to an equation.
Do not omit opportunity cost.

units.source_excerpt: The government must take this item into account in its revenue and expenditure plan, carefully assess the probability of environmental damage, and prevent the chain reaction caused by reduced environmental benefits.
units.function: Close the proposed feedback section with risk assessment and prevention.

features.quantitative_role: calls for risk input absent from current model

units.reusable_pattern: Include [contingent cost] in the plan, estimate its probability, and identify the downstream state changes it prevents.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim prevention without a risk model.
Do not hide the missing feedback implementation.

units.source_excerpt: In the model sensitivity analysis, we mainly analyzed the effects of small perturbations in the proportion of tourists, tax rate and tourist consumption, on the total number of tourists and total benefits.
units.function: Declare perturbed factors and response outputs before interpreting plots.
units.reusable_pattern: Perturb [factors] locally and report effects on [decision output] and [objective output], holding [other dimensions] fixed.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call local one-factor sweeps global robustness.
Do not omit fixed factors and ranges.

units.source_excerpt: The conclusions that can be drawn from the two graphs on the left are that the greatest number of tourists visit the glacier when the proportion visiting the glacier is roughly equal to the proportion visiting the other attractions, and the number required for optimal performance decreases as the tax rate increases.
units.function: Read panels in a stable left-to-right order with conditional statements.
units.reusable_pattern: Reading panels in order, state [factor condition] -> [response], then compare whether the direction persists across cases.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use effect without a controlled contrast.
Do not report only favorable directions.

units.source_excerpt: When tourist spending is below 4,000 USD, the number of tourists continues to increase while performance per tourist rises slowly. Subsequently, when spending exceeds 4,000 USD, the number of tourists decreases sharply and total benefits decrease in the same trend.
units.function: Describe a response regime before and after a visible turning point.
units.reusable_pattern: Below [turning point], [responses]; subsequently, above it, [responses].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a visually chosen turning point an estimated elasticity threshold.
Do not infer consumer categories without data.

units.source_excerpt: The results are as follows: as tourist proportion increases, social, environmental, economic, and total benefits all increase; as tax rate increases, environmental benefits rise while economic, social, and total benefits decline; as tourist consumption increases, total benefits first increase and then decrease.
units.function: Summarize factor-by-objective directions in a compact parallel list.

features.clause_structure: colon plus three semicolon-separated as clauses
features.transition: The results are as follows; as; while

units.reusable_pattern: For each factor, list the direction of every objective; preserve mixed and nonmonotonic responses.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not replace effect sizes with directions when importance is claimed.
Do not call deterministic sweeps statistical.

units.source_excerpt: Computational Feasibility: The model employs nonlinear marginal effect formulations and integrates economic, social, and ecological dimensions into a unified framework.
units.function: Name a strength and immediately identify the design feature supporting it.
units.reusable_pattern: [Strength label]: [specific design operation], which supports [bounded benefit].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not equate SLSQP execution with theoretical rigor.
Do not say feasible without runtime or convergence evidence.

units.source_excerpt: Holistic Cost Internalization: Social policies and environmental impacts are consolidated into quantifiable metrics. Generalizability and Practicality: The framework is adaptable to other tourism destinations.
units.function: Continue strengths with parallel labels and one defining operation each.
units.reusable_pattern: Use parallel [strength label]: [operation] -> [scoped value] blocks.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call arbitrary monetization holistic.
Do not call one second city generalizability.

units.source_excerpt: Temporal Simplification: The model ignores time-lag effects in tourism's response to policy changes. Spatiotemporal Narrowness: External competition, infrastructure decay, and seasonal fluctuations are excluded.
units.function: Pair each limitation with the omitted process and a concrete extension family.
units.reusable_pattern: [Limitation]: [omitted mechanism], which may [consequence]; extend with [method/data].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat a future-method name as a completed fix.
Do not hide limitations after strong transfer claims.

units.source_excerpt: The model provides a practical tool in places like Juneau, which balances simplicity with real-world applicability, addressing economic, social, and environmental benefit through hidden-cost monetization. The fixed system approach allows quick policy solutions.
units.function: Compress the paper around architecture, intended use, and scope.

features.clause_structure: main claim plus relative and participial elaboration
features.transition: The model provides; Its strength lies

units.reusable_pattern: Conclude with [artifact], [dimensions handled], [decision use], and [scope boundary] in that order.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not strengthen local simulation into real-world applicability.
Do not repeat global/Pareto claims unsupported by the solver evidence.

units.source_excerpt: After expanding the model to Jiuzhaigou, China, although both locations are affected by overtourism, the measures adopted differ due to the distinct geographical attributes of the two areas. Table 3 compares similar parts, different parts, key parameters, constraint factors, optimized factors, and promotion measures.

features.clause_structure: After/although frame followed by full-page matrix

units.reusable_pattern: For transfer, compare [shared structure], [context differences], [parameters], [constraints], and [case-specific decisions] in one matrix.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not fill matrix cells with unsupported qualitative claims.
Do not merge evidence across cases.

units.source_excerpt: The city of Juneau is attracting the attention and love of tourists with its beautiful natural landscape and comfortable living environment, which undoubtedly brings great economic benefits. However, the rapid increase in tourists is damaging natural resources and disturbing residents.
units.function: Open the stakeholder memo with shared value followed by the management problem.
units.reusable_pattern: [Place/system] creates [shared value]; however, [trend] now imposes [specific harms].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use decorative praise instead of evidence.
Do not overstate causality.

units.source_excerpt: Our assessment of the current state of tourism development indicates that if no management measures are taken, the number of visitors will remain above 1.6 million for the next decade and the Mendenhall Glacier will recede from its current viewpoints.
units.function: Convert the problem into a conditional urgency statement before recommendations.

features.clause_structure: indicates-that with if clause and coordinated forecasts

units.reusable_pattern: Under a clearly sourced no-action scenario, [decision variable] follows [path] and [consequence] follows [path]; therefore action is needed.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not include forecasts absent from the model.
Do not turn contextual glacier equations into city-specific dates.

units.source_excerpt: Measure 1: Increase Visitor Dispersion. Methods: Increase publicity for niche attractions and limit visitor flow or periodically close popular scenic spots. Effect: The greater the dispersion of tourists, the more balanced the number accepted by each attraction.
units.function: Package one recommendation as measure, methods, and modeled effect.

features.clause_structure: three labeled lines with comparative effect

units.reusable_pattern: Measure [i]: [action]. Methods: [implementable controls]. Effect under the model: [scoped response].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim real-world effect without implementation evidence.
Do not omit distributional harms.

units.source_excerpt: Measure 2: Increase Tourist Consumption. Methods: Increase tax rates and commodity prices at scenic spots. Effect: When the tax rate and prices increase, the number of tourists decreases and the total benefits increases.
units.function: Repeat the recommendation block for a price/tax lever.
units.reusable_pattern: Repeat the Measure-Methods-Effect syntax so recommendations are scan-comparable.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not recommend a tax value that conflicts with units or the tested range.
Do not combine taxes and prices as one isolated factor.

units.source_excerpt: Measure 3: Determine the Optimal Number of Tourists. Method: Analyze the number of tourists when the total benefits is maximum through Pareto optimality. Effect: Ensure sustainable development and promote the maximization of social benefits.
units.function: Close recommendations with the primary decision variable and intended objective.
units.reusable_pattern: End with the primary decision: [value/range], [selection criterion], and [scoped consequence].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not relabel total-benefit optimum as social-benefit maximum.
Do not call the result Pareto optimality without evidence.
